stem: "Authorities have to focus on just stopping the spread, rather than putting the fire out." This means that the authorities:
optA: Want only to slow down the spread of fire
optB: Do not want to put the fires out
optC: Want to stop the fires from spreading first and then put them out
optD: Want to put out the fires once and for all
context:
Read the passage carefully and choose the best answer to each question out of the four alternatives.

Since September, at least 25 people have died and thousands have been made homeless. Every state and territory in Australia has experienced fires this summer. But the biggest fires burn along stretches of the eastern and southern coast, where most of the population lives. This includes areas around sydney and Adelaide. More than 6.3 million hectares ( 63,000 sq km or 15.6 million acres) have been burned so far - one hectare is roughly the size of a sports field. To put that in perspective, around 800,000 hectares were engulfed in a bush fire in 2018 in California. Australia has always experienced bushfires - it has a "fire season". But this year they are a lot worse than normal. Fires are usually caused by lightning strikes or accidentally by a spark-but some fires are also started deliberately. This year, a natural weather phenomenon known as the 'Indian Ocean Dipole' has meant a hot, dry spell across the country. This year, Australia twice set a new temperature record: an average maximum of \(41.9^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\) was recorded on 18 December. That comes on top of a long period of drought. Scientists have long warned that this hotter, drier climate will contribute to fires becoming more frequent and more intense. The more extreme weather patterns and higher temperatures increase the risk of bushfires and allow them to spread faster and wider. Fire fighters are spraying water and fire retardant from planes and helicopters as well as from the ground. But fighting bushfires is extremely difficult and often authorities have to focus on just stopping the spread, rather than putting the fire out. The spread can for instance be best contained by digging earth boundaries to stop the flames from spreading. The priority is saving lives. Professional fire fighters are the first in line to battle the flames, but they are outnumbered by the thousands of volunteers. Three of them have died. There's also help coming from abroad: the US, Canada and New Zealand have sent firefighters to help. Australia's police, military and navy are involved in rescue and evacuation efforts. While people can flee the fires and are being evacuated, if need be, the flames are devastating wildlife in the affected areas. One study estimated that half a billion animals have died in New South wales alone. Zookeepers take animals home to save them from fire, but the fires don't only kill animals directly, they also destroy the habitat, leaving the survivors vulnerable even when the fires have gone. So, the true scale of loss isn't yet clear. Experts say more than 100,000 cows and sheep may also have been lost, which is devastating for farmers. Each state runs its own emergency operation, but Prime Minister Scott Morrison has promised better funding for fire-fighting and payouts for volunteer firefighters, and an additional A$2 billion ( $1.4 billion; \(\pounds\)1 billion) for the recovery. But the national government has come under strong criticism from its opponents that it has not been doing enough against climate change. The country is one of the world's biggest per capita greenhouse gas emitters but under international agreements it has committed itself to reduction targets.
solution: The quoted line sets two tasks against each other and says which gets the effort first, containment ahead of extinguishing, and the passage immediately explains how, by digging earth boundaries to stop the flames spreading. That is a statement about order and priority, not about giving up on the fire, so the reading that puts containment first and extinguishing afterwards is the faithful one. The tempting distractor replaces 'stopping' with 'slowing down', which weakens what the passage actually claims, and the option saying the authorities do not want to put the fires out mistakes a practical necessity for a wish. Matches option C.
subject: English

stem: Sachin says, "I am enjoying my holiday."
optA: Sachin says that he enjoys his holiday.
optB: Sachin says that he was enjoying his holiday.
optC: Sachin says that he is enjoying his holiday.
optD: Sachin says that he has been enjoying his holiday.
context: In the following questions, a sentence has been given in Direct or Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect or Direct speech
solution: The reporting verb 'says' is in the present tense, and a present-tense reporting verb causes no backshift in the reported clause. The present continuous 'am enjoying' therefore stays present continuous, and only the pronouns change, giving 'he is enjoying his holiday'. The versions with 'was enjoying', 'enjoys' and 'has been enjoying' all alter a tense that should have been left alone. Matches option C.

stem: Sapna said to her friend, 'What a hectic day!'
optA: Sapna exclaimed sorrowfully that it can be a hectic day.
optB: Sapna told her that it was a hectic day.
optC: Sapna said joyfully that it was a hectic day.
optD: Sapna exclaimed that it was a hectic day.
context: In the following questions, a sentence has been given in Direct or Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect or Direct speech
solution: 'What a hectic day!' is an exclamation, so the reporting verb becomes 'exclaimed' and the exclamatory structure is rewritten as a statement. Since 'said' is past, the implied 'is' backshifts to 'was', giving 'exclaimed that it was a hectic day'. One distractor drops the exclamation entirely by using 'told', another attaches an emotion the original never states, and calling a hectic day joyful contradicts it. Matches option D.

context: In the following questions, a sentence has been given in Direct or Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect or Direct speech
solution: An imperative delivered by a superior with an exclamation mark is a command, so the reporting verb becomes 'ordered' and the imperative turns into a to-infinitive. The possessive must also shift out of the listener's viewpoint, so 'your emails' becomes 'her emails'. One distractor leaves 'your' unchanged, another uses 'demanded' with a that-clause, which is not how that verb takes a person as object, and 'requested' softens an instruction that was issued as an order. stem: Teacher said to him, 'Why don't you work hard?'

stem: He said to me, "Is the hospital near the shopping mall?"

stem: \(37^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\) temperature is equal to

stem: Minimum possible temperature is

stem: Dimensional formula of impulse is

stem: Melting of ice at its melting point is a

stem: Which one of the following is correct ? Large aperture telescopes are used for
solution: The finest detail a telescope can separate is limited by diffraction at its opening, and that limiting angle is inversely proportional to the aperture, so widening the aperture resolves closer pairs of objects and gathers more light besides. Magnification is fixed by the ratio of the objective and eyepiece focal lengths and can be changed simply by swapping the eyepiece, so it is not a reason to build a large aperture; and a larger lens is harder to figure accurately and shows more aberration, not less. Matches option A.

stem: Which one of the following is the correct statements ? If pieces of copper and germanium are cooled from room temperature to liquid nitrogen temperature , then the
optC: resistance of copper decreases while that of germanium increases
optD: resistance of copper increases while that of germanium decreases
solution: Copper is a metal, and cooling it quietens the thermal vibration of its lattice so that the free electrons are scattered less often; its resistance therefore falls as the temperature drops. Germanium is a semiconductor, and cooling leaves far fewer electrons with enough energy to cross the band gap into the conduction band, so the number of charge carriers collapses and its resistance rises steeply. The two materials therefore move in opposite directions, which is the whole point of the comparison. Matches option C.

stem: If an \(\alpha\)- particle is projected normally through a uniform magnetic filed , then the path of the \(\alpha\)-particle inside the field will be
solution: The magnetic force on a moving charge acts at right angles to both the velocity and the field, so it can turn the particle but can never speed it up or slow it down. A force of constant magnitude that stays perpendicular to the velocity is exactly a centripetal force, so the alpha particle, entering normally, is bent into a circle of radius \(r = mv/(qB)\) in the plane perpendicular to the field. A parabola would need a constant force in a fixed direction, as in projectile motion, which is not the case here. Matches option A.

stem:
Following statements are made in connection with carbon dioxide (\(\mathrm{CO_{2}}\))
1. \(\mathrm{CO_{2}}\) is a poisonous gas.
2. \(\mathrm{CO_{2}}\) is an acidic oxide.
3. \(\mathrm{CO_{2}}\) turns limewater milky.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
solution: Carbon dioxide is an acidic oxide, dissolving in water to give carbonic acid, and it turns limewater milky by forming a suspension of insoluble calcium carbonate, so the second and third statements are both correct. It is not poisonous: it suffocates only by displacing air when it collects in high concentration. The genuinely toxic oxide of carbon is carbon monoxide, which binds to haemoglobin and blocks the transport of oxygen, and confusing the two is what makes the first statement tempting. Matches option B.

solution: Graphite is one of the allotropes of carbon, so it is built from a single kind of atom and is an element. Alumina is aluminium oxide and silica is silicon dioxide, each a compound of two different elements, while brass is an alloy of copper and zinc and so is a mixture. Matches option C.

Which of the statements about glass are correct?
1. Glass is a super-cooled liquid having infinite viscosity.
2. Violet coloured glass is obtained by adding \(\mathrm{MnO_{2}}\).
3. Glass is a man-made silicate.
4. Glass is a crystalline substance

solution: Glass is a man-made silicate, produced by fusing sand with soda and lime, so the third statement holds. It has no long-range ordered lattice and is amorphous, not crystalline, so the fourth statement fails and any option containing it can be dropped at once. It is conventionally described as a super-cooled liquid of extremely high, effectively infinite, viscosity, and manganese dioxide added to the melt gives the violet tint, so the first two statements stand. Matches option C.

stem: Which one among the following is not a property of salt ?
optA: Salts have ordered packing arrangements called lattices
optB: Salts have low melting points but high boiling points
optD: Salts conduct electricity when dissolved in water or even in the molten state
solution: Salts are ionic solids and the electrostatic attraction binding their lattices is strong, so a great deal of energy is needed to pull the ions apart; their melting points are high, not low. That statement is therefore the false one. The ordered lattice, the brittleness that follows when a blow slides like charges opposite one another, and the conduction of electricity once the ions are freed by melting or dissolving are all genuine properties of salts. Matches option B.

solution: Hydration is the taking up of water into a mineral's own structure, which is a chemical change, but the swelling that goes with it sets up a mechanical stress that flakes and splits the rock, so the process works in both ways at once. Carbonation is purely chemical, the carbonic acid in rainwater attacking limestone, while the growth of salt crystals and exfoliation by repeated heating and cooling are purely mechanical.
